layout_dets.text: AbstractAn electrode kinetic model for pit initiation has been described in terms of the charge on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: oxide surface and the pH of zero charge parameter. The model takes into account adsorption of chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions on the oxide surface, penctration of chloride ions through the oxide film via vacancy transport, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: localized dissolution of aluminum at the metal/oxide interface in three consecutive single electron transfer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steps. Mathematical expressions are derived which agree with the experimentally determined variation in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting potential with chloride ion concentration at constant pH and with the variation in pitting potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with pH at constant chloride ion concentration.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Previous work in this laboratory1 and by Bargeron and Givens² has shown that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion pits on aluminum develop into blisters beneath the air-formed oxide film.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The propagation of such corrosion pits involves the hydrolysis of aluminum ions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under a restricted exchange of local and bulk electrolytes, resulting in a localized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: area of low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leading to pit propagation and eventual rupture of the blister.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The mechanism of pit initiation leading to the above situation is not as clear,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: although there is considerable evidence to show that aggressive anions, such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chlorides, assist the breakdown of passive oxide films. For example, several different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: groups have found chloride ion incorporation within passive films on aluminum using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: XPS,4 and Bargeron and Givens² have detected the presence of chloride around

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the periphery of blisters which develop later in the pitting process. The exact detailed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanism of pit initiation is still somewhat uncertain, however, because there are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: several possible mechanisms by which chloride ions may penetrate the oxide film and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assist the attack of the underlying substrate. These possiblities involve: (i) transport

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of chloride ions through the oxide film; and (ii) localized film dissolution or thinning.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It is generally agreed that the first step in the initiation process involves adsorption of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride ions on the oxide surface.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Despite this lack of detailed understanding as to the exact mechanism of pitting, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is well known that there exists a critical pitting potential above which corrosion pits

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initiate and then propagate. This critical pitting potential, which is associated with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the initiation stage of pitting, is a function of chloride concentration but is indepen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dent of pH.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The purpose of this communication is to provide an electrode kinetic description

layout_dets.text: of pit initiation for aluminum (having an air-formed oxide film), taking into account

layout_dets.text: Additional comments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Another possible mechanism by which Cl⁻ ions breach the oxide film is by film

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thinning, i.e. local dissolution of the oxide film.30 If the oxide film is thinned locally in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a channel extending only part way through the thickness of the oxide film, then there

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: still exists a remaining part of the oxide film through which Cl~ ions may pcnetrate by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the mechanism considered above, so that the above treatment will still hold.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, the observation that blisters develop beneath the oxide film, on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aluminum¹² suggests that the oxide film is not dissolved away locally down to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: underlying metal substrate in order for a corrosion pit to initiate.

layout_dets.text: SUMMARY

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An electrode kinetic model for pit initiation has been described taking into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: account adsorption of chloride ions on the oxide surface, penetration through the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: oxide film by means of oxygen vacancies and dissolution of the underlying substrate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to initiate a corrosion pit at the metal/oxide interface. Mathematical expressions are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: derived which agree with the variation in pitting potential with chloride ion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentration at constant pH, and with the variation in pitting potential with pH at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constant chloride ion concentration.
